title: Ratelens MRP Mismatch Index (India)
subtitle: Amazon vs Flipkart: the same product with two different declared MRPs
description:
Monthly frozen editions of the Ratelens MRP Mismatch Index. In the August 2026 edition, 54 products carried a different declared MRP across Amazon.in and Flipkart; in 15 of them the selling price was effectively identical, leaving the discount badge as the only difference.

Under India's Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, MRP is a property of the product, not the shop. Where two platforms declare different MRPs, the advertised '% off' is calculated from a figure at least one of them has wrong.

Products are matched on manufacturer model code, not title text. Each edition is frozen on the last day of its month and never rewritten, so a cited figure stays true.

IMPORTANT: this data does not show WHICH platform is wrong — with two sources it shows only that both cannot be right. The can_name column is false in exactly those cases. It does not establish intent; a wrong MRP may be a stale entry or a pack revision.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Manufacturer model code used to match the product across platforms.

fields.name: a_price
fields.description: Selling price observed on the Amazon.in listing, INR.

fields.name: a_mrp
fields.description: Maximum Retail Price declared by the Amazon.in listing, INR.

fields.name: a_off
fields.description: Discount percentage advertised on the Amazon.in listing.

fields.name: f_price
fields.description: Selling price observed on the Flipkart listing, INR.

fields.name: f_mrp
fields.description: Maximum Retail Price declared by the Flipkart listing, INR.

fields.name: f_off
fields.description: Discount percentage advertised on the Flipkart listing.

fields.name: gap
fields.description: Percentage difference between the two declared MRPs.

fields.name: grade
fields.description: Confidence that the mismatch is real: High, Medium or Low.

fields.name: can_name
fields.description: True only when a third listing lets a majority identify which platform is the outlier. When false, the data shows the two declared MRPs cannot both be correct, but not which one is wrong.
